title: IBM, IonQ, Diraq, and Atom Computing advance to DARPA's quantum hardware testing stage
key_facts: DARPA is awarding up to $300 million each to IBM, IonQ, Diraq and Atom Computing to prepare their quantum hardware for independent testing
The four have entered Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative; Microsoft and PsiQuantum were already in Stage C
Approaches differ: Atom neutral atoms, Diraq silicon spin qubits, IBM superconducting circuits, IonQ trapped ions
The initiative judges whether vendors have a credible plan to build a sufficiently powerful quantum computer by 2033 (analyst Bob Sutor)
Google has chosen not to take part (Sutor)
Sutor warns selection does not guarantee companies meet roadmaps; Gartner predicts half of quantum startups will be out of business by 2030
quote_evidence: The U.S. government’s Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, or DARPA, is awarding up to $300 million each to four companies to help them get their quantum computing hardware ready for independent testing.
“This doesn’t guarantee companies will meet their roadmaps or avoid or overcome unforeseen technical roadblocks,” says Sutor.
why_it_matters_hint: The awards mean outside experts will test the machines of four leading builders, giving buyers more than vendor claims to plan against.
notes: Network World's own reporting with company and analyst quotes; 'up to' $300m is a ceiling.
